after.text:
The celebrated Riemann hypothesis (abbreviated as the RH hereafter)
to the effect that all nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta-function ζ(s) (s =
σ + it) lie on the critical line σ = 1/2 has been the driving force of the
developments of modern mathematics in general and of prime number theory

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The useful object is the discrepancy coordinate delta_nu: it compares each ordered reduced fraction with the uniformly spaced point of the same rank. The mediant construction and denominator-stratified count explain the discrete geometry whose deviation is later measured.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit defines the Farey sequence of order x, its augmentation by 0/1, recursive insertion of admissible mediants, its totient count Phi(x), and delta_nu = rho_nu - nu/Phi(x).
directed.conceptual_reading: Rank coordinates turn an irregular arithmetic point set into a perturbation of a uniform grid. Delta_nu retains order-sensitive displacement while forgetting the individual numerator-denominator description unless that data is supplied separately.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is from reduced fractions organized by denominator to an ordered point configuration with discrepancy coordinates; mediants explain how configurations at successive orders are related.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is setup, not an RH criterion or a discrepancy estimate. The concrete F_2-to-F_3 example illustrates the insertion rule but proves no asymptotic claim.
directed.uncertainty: The structural definitions are clear; flattened subscripts and the displayed constant in the Phi(x) asymptotic should be checked before exact reuse.

supported: The span defines the ordered reduced fractions, augmentation by 0/1, mediant insertion rule, totient-based cardinality, and the indexed discrepancy delta_nu.
The candidate correctly treats the F_2-to-F_3 construction as an illustration rather than an asymptotic result or RH criterion.
inference: Viewing delta_nu as rank-sensitive displacement from a uniform grid is a useful and source-grounded interpretation.
unsupported_or_imported: The claim that delta_nu forgets the numerator-denominator description unless that data is separately supplied is misleading: together with nu and Phi(x), delta_nu recovers rho_nu, whose reduced numerator and denominator are determined.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The phrase 'discrete geometry' is interpretive but remains tied to the mediant and ordering constructions.
context_or_ocr_risk: Flattened fraction subscripts and the Phi(x) asymptotic make literal formula reuse unsafe; the candidate appropriately flags this.
missed_mechanism: The information retained by an indexed discrepancy should be distinguished from the information in an unindexed scalar delta value.
revision_instructions: Remove the asserted loss of numerator-denominator information, or narrow it to delta viewed without its rank, order, and Phi(x) metadata; retain the rank-displacement interpretation and existing formula caveat.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Two classical arithmetic error terms provide interchangeable downstream targets: cancellation in the summatory Mobius function and square-root error in Chebyshev's function. Later Farey identities can therefore inherit RH equivalence by reducing to either target.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit defines M(x) as the summatory Mobius function and psi(x) through the von Mangoldt function, then states that RH is equivalent respectively to M(x)=O(x^(1/2+epsilon)) and psi(x)=x+O(x^(1/2+epsilon)).
directed.conceptual_reading: The same zero-location statement is represented as cancellation in a signed divisor statistic or as an error term in weighted prime counting. These are calibration endpoints rather than independent evidence.
directed.representation_or_bridge: M(x) and psi(x)-x are bridge statistics to which later Farey, Kubert, and special-function sums are algebraically reduced.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The equivalences are stated here, not proved in this span, and they do not make an arbitrary Farey statistic RH-equivalent.
directed.uncertainty: The prose and roles are clear; typographically flattened exponents should be verified for exact quotation.

supported: The span defines M(x), Lambda, and psi(x), and states the two square-root-error formulations equivalent to RH.
The candidate correctly notes that these equivalences are stated rather than proved in this unit.
inference: Treating the two estimates as different arithmetic representations of the same zero-location condition is a defensible interpretation.
unsupported_or_imported: Claims that later Farey, Kubert, and special-function identities reduce to these targets are not established in this span or its bounded nearby context.
Calling them 'calibration endpoints' is experimental vocabulary not supplied by the source.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Interchangeable downstream targets' overstates what the local evidence itself establishes.
context_or_ocr_risk: The exponents are flattened but legible; exact quotation still requires verification.
revision_instructions: Confine the reading to the two stated RH-equivalent arithmetic error estimates and their contrasting Mobius-cancellation versus prime-counting roles; remove claims about later reductions and calibration use.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Quadratic and cubic moments collapse to the same RH signal
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Shows that distinct whole-interval power-moment deviations are affine multiples of S(x), hence equivalent to RH by a common hidden arithmetic statistic.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Residue extraction and telescoping preserve cancellation exponents
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Shows that removing multiples of a modulus and comparing scaled arguments can be inverted by a finite telescoping series, so the transformed bound is equivalent to the original S_s or Chebyshev bound.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Centering each truncated Farey sum by its actual local count h(xi) rather than by a fixed expected count isolates a controllable quadratic identity. The adaptive center absorbs fluctuations in how many Farey points fall before xi.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Proposition 2 rewrites the sum over rho_nu<=xi of rho_nu-h(xi)/(2Phi(x)) using a Phi(x)xi^2 term, h(xi)^2/(2Phi(x)), Bernoulli-weighted Mertens sums, and S(x). The proof subtracts the local-count center from the k=1 moment formula.
directed.conceptual_reading: Adaptive centering separates displacement of the observed points from count discrepancy. It preserves the short-interval arithmetic structure that fixed endpoint constants can mix with uncontrolled residue errors.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge combines the first-moment identity with h(xi), producing the centered statistic used by the fractional-part kernel and rational-endpoint criteria.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The identity does not itself bound the terms, and changing the center changes which count errors remain. Exact coefficients are necessary for any quantitative use.
directed.uncertainty: The algebraic role is clear; flattened fractions in the display require scan verification for exact normalization.

supported: Proposition 2 rewrites the locally centered partial Farey sum in terms of Phi(x)xi^2, h(xi)^2/Phi(x), Bernoulli-weighted Mertens sums, and S(x).
The proof obtains the identity by subtracting the local-count center from the k=1 moment formula.
inference: Adaptive centering can reasonably be described as separating location information from fluctuation in the number of points before xi.
unsupported_or_imported: The claim that fixed endpoint constants leave uncontrolled residue errors belongs to a later unit and is not supported by this span or its bounded nearby context.
Specific assertions that this identity is used by a fractional-part kernel and rational-endpoint criteria import later developments.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The candidate's core interpretation is substantive, but its downstream comparisons make the unit appear to prove more than an algebraic setup.
context_or_ocr_risk: Flattened fractions make all exact coefficients and normalization formula-sensitive; the candidate flags this.
revision_instructions: Keep the local-count centering identity and the count-versus-location interpretation, but delete the claims about fixed-centering residue obstructions and named later criteria unless they are separately source-linked.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Kubert identities turn Farey averages into gcd-weighted sums
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Transforms single and pairwise Farey averages of a Kubert function into Mertens-weighted gcd sums, combining distribution identities with the Farey Möbius transform.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The Kubert distribution identity restricts a broad-looking function class to a two-dimensional parity split. This classification makes even and odd components the natural coordinates for deciding what survives symmetric Farey averaging.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The unit defines K_s by a distribution identity, states that it is two-dimensional with one even and one odd generator, gives polylogarithm and Hurwitz-zeta bases in stated parameter ranges, and records conditions for extension from (0,1) to the circle.
directed.conceptual_reading: A functional equation compresses functions into a small representation space. Reflection parity is structural rather than cosmetic because the Farey set is symmetric and can annihilate the odd direction.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Polylogarithm and Hurwitz-zeta realizations provide analytic coordinate systems for the abstract Kubert space, while circle extension permits evaluation at translated Farey points.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The basis descriptions have excluded parameter values and extension hypotheses. Dimension and parity classification do not themselves imply RH-sensitive estimates.
directed.uncertainty: The structural statements are legible; exact domains, normalizations, and special-function series should be checked against the page image.

supported: The span defines the Kubert distribution identity, states dim_C K_s=2 with even and odd generators, supplies polylogarithm and Hurwitz-zeta bases in restricted parameter ranges, and gives circle-extension conditions.
The candidate preserves the important parameter and extension caveats.
inference: Describing the functional equation as compressing the class into a two-coordinate representation is a sound reading of the dimension statement.
unsupported_or_imported: Claims that Farey symmetry annihilates the odd direction and that parity decides what survives Farey averaging are not established in this unit or its bounded nearby context.
Saying circle extension permits evaluation at translated Farey points anticipates a later application rather than describing the local theorem.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The spontaneous reading turns a structural classification into a downstream selection result before that result is proved.
context_or_ocr_risk: The special-function series, exceptional parameters, and normalizations are flattened and require scan verification.
revision_instructions: Restrict the conceptual reading to the two-dimensional parity decomposition, analytic bases, and extension theorem; remove the claims about Farey averaging or label them only in a separately supported cross-unit synthesis.

unit_result_entry.title: Half-interval tangent sums encode a Chebyshev scale difference
unit_result_entry.why_material: Converts a half-interval Farey sum of log tan into psi(x)-psi(x/2), whose square-root error is equivalent to RH by the estimate-preserving telescoping principle.

neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Uses real and imaginary parts of polylogarithms to express the same RH signal in Bernoulli-polynomial and Clausen-function representations.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Generalized Dedekind correlations and their cyclic three-term law
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Introduces the Bernoulli correlation needed for Farey discrepancies and states the cyclic three-term relation whose gcd terms ultimately collapse to Franel's formula.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Finite tangent products make the half-interval kernel collapse to log n on odd denominators and zero on even ones. The Farey transform therefore yields the scale difference psi(x)-psi(x/2), whose cancellation bound can be telescopically inverted.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Proposition 4 expresses the half-interval Farey sum of log tan(pi rho_nu) as one half of psi(x)-psi(x/2) minus a constant, and states that its centered square-root estimate is equivalent to RH. The proof uses finite tangent products and Lemma 3; a cotangent analogue is recorded.
directed.conceptual_reading: A special-function product selects denominator parity, turning geometric truncation at one half into an arithmetic dilation difference. The selected difference retains the full growth exponent because of the earlier telescoping principle.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Finite tangent products bridge residue sums to log n; the Mobius transform and divisor identity bridge log n to the Chebyshev scale difference.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The exact centering constant and one-half factors matter, and similar behavior is not established for arbitrary trigonometric functions or endpoints.
directed.uncertainty: The Chebyshev difference and proof chain are legible; product displays and constants remain formula-sensitive.

supported: Proposition 4 expresses the half-interval log-tangent Farey sum as one half of psi(x)-psi(x/2), with the displayed constant, and states the correctly centered RH-equivalent estimate.
The proof uses finite tangent products, Lemma 3, and a divisor/logarithm conversion; a cotangent analogue is recorded.
inference: Interpreting the denominator-parity selector as a dilation difference is supported by the proof and the preceding telescoping principle.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous reading says the finite kernel equals log n for odd denominators, but the displayed identity gives (1/2)log n; this loses a material normalization factor.
context_or_ocr_risk: Product displays and constants are formula-sensitive, making preservation of the one-half factors especially important.
revision_instructions: Change the spontaneous reading to say the kernel gives one half of log n for odd denominators and zero for even denominators; preserve the one-half factor in the resulting Chebyshev scale difference and the stated centering constant.
